subtype: Approach: turns each imagined failure into a preventive step [Action]
passage:
Hi Sonali,

Before Saturday, can we try something? Imagine it's Sunday evening and we lost. Why? I wrote down two big reasons. One: the venue's internet is patchy, and our model needs a download. Two: I'm the only one who has written any code so far, so if I get stuck or fall ill, we're finished. Here's what I've done about them. I booked a phone data plan for the weekend and already saved the model files on the laptop. And I split the app into three parts: mine is the model, yours is the front end, and Ravi has the data cleaning. Can you look at the split and tell me if the front end is too much?

Tejas

qa.a: Tejas is worried about being the only coder, since getting stuck or ill would leave the team unable to finish.

qa.q: What other step could the team add to lower the risk further?
qa.a: The team could hold a short check-in each evening to see who is stuck, since a problem found early is easier to share out.

qa.q: How might Sonali feel about the front-end part?
qa.a: Sonali may feel a little pressed by the workload but relieved that the coding is now shared.

grounding: Shows a student team imagining losing a hackathon, listing weak internet and one person doing all the coding, then booking a data plan and splitting the work among three.
